concepts.why: The patient has a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance, consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
The patient has a history of fever and cough, and bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance, consistent with ARDS.
The patient has a history of fever and cough, and elevated WBC and CRP, consistent with VAP.
The patient has a history of fever and cough, and elevated WBC and CRP, consistent with sepsis.
The patient has an elevated APTT, consistent with DIC.
The patient has diffuse edema of the intestine, including the transverse colon, consistent with AKI.
The patient has a history of dialysis-dependent nephropathy, consistent with ESRD.
The patient has diffuse edema of the intestine, including the transverse colon, consistent with gastrointestinal edema.
The patient has a low blood pressure, consistent with hypotension.
The patient has a rapid heart rate, consistent with tachycardia.

rationales.F02: The patient's symptoms of fever and cough are consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia and ARDS.
rationales.F03: The confirmation of SARS-CoV-2 infection by nasopharyngeal PCR strongly supports the diagnosis of COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F06: The patient's tachycardia is a common finding in sepsis and COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F08: The elevated WBC count is a common finding in bacterial infections, including ventilator-associated pneumonia, and in sepsis.
rationales.F09: The elevated CRP level is a common finding in bacterial infections, including ventilator-associated pneumonia, and in sepsis.
rationales.F10: The bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance on chest CT are characteristic of COVID-19 pneumonia and ARDS.
rationales.F11: The diffuse edema of the intestine, including the transverse colon, may be related to sepsis or COVID-19.
rationales.F12: The prolonged APTT suggests coagulopathy, which is a common finding in DIC.
